findings.description: The sixth location is now enumerated everywhere it needed to be, and it is the one location C-8's check cannot reach. The rubric is sentence-shaped — "for each of the six locations, quote the shipped sentence and name the line of `lint-scope.sh` that decides it" — and location six is a three-row table plus a sentence. A checker following that rubric literally quotes `:21`, ties it to the v1 routing line, finds it true after the fix, and passes the location without ever having looked at the table. That is precisely the outcome the clause text goes to some length to forbid: the text says outright that the table is part of the location and not context for it, and then hands the checker a method that only tests the prose. Worse, the constraint you chose *in place of* specifying the form — "after your edit, a reader must be able to learn from this table what a v1 file actually gets" — appears only at T-003.md:93, in the worker's excerpt. It is in neither C-8's check nor T-003's C-8 `check_method`, which reproduces the constitution's sentence-shaped rubric verbatim. So the worker is bound by a constraint its checker has no instruction to apply. A clause requirement with no check method is the defect CON-audit exists to catch, and it is load-bearing here because the table is the artifact a reader consults first.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:147 (C-8 check) and T-003.md:13-17 (C-8 check_method) both read "quote the shipped sentence and name the line of lint-scope.sh that decides it," with no limb for a table. The reader test is at T-003.md:93 only. Compare constitution.md:144, which correctly states the requirement: "The table is part of the location, not context for it … there is no Links column, so after the fix the document's most authoritative artifact about generations still answers 'what does the lint do to a v1 file' with 'nothing.'" Suggested limb, to be added to C-8's check and mirrored into T-003's check_method: "For location six, additionally apply the reader test directly — read the generation table as shipped, with nothing else, and state what the lint checks on a file carrying no `schema` key. If that answer is 'nothing,' or cannot be given from the table alone, the location fails no matter how the sentence beneath it reads." That is falsifiable, needs no judgment about form, and is the same test the worker is held to.

findings.description: Ruling on the latitude question: keep it, and do not specify the shape — conditional on the finding above being repaired, because latitude is only sound when the constraint standing in for a specification is itself checkable. Three reasons the latitude is right on the merits. A Links column is the obvious specification and it is probably the worse artifact: rows two and three would both read "checked" and are unaffected by this job, so the column exists to carry one new fact and widens a table that currently reads cleanly at two columns. The task is worker-craft on opus precisely so that form is the worker's judgment to exercise; specifying it spends the tier and then overrides it. And a bad-form repair is not unchecked — C-10 already polices register, reason-alongside-rule, and the two typographic rules, so the failure mode latitude opens is narrower than it looks. What the clause must not leave open is the *outcome*, and the reader test closes that. Specify the test, not the shape.
findings.evidence: T-003.md:93 offers "a Links column, a footnote, a reworked sentence" and requires the worker to say why in the prose, which C-10's reason-alongside-rule check at constitution.md:155 already enforces independently. machine-contracts.md:13-17 rows two and three are unchanged by this job.

findings.description: The search is closed at six, and I am now saying that as a bounded result rather than as confidence. You were right that a third method was owed, and right that it had to fail differently. I ran three prongs, none of which depends on how a claim happens to be phrased. (1) Code-first. The lint has exactly three generation-dependent branches: `has_schema_key` at :424, `has_v1_body` at :451, and the `memory_type` guard at :461, which is a file-kind test rather than a generation test. T-001 changes only the first. So the set of claims that *can* be falsified by this job is not open-ended — it is any passage describing what a file carrying no `schema` key receives, and nothing else. Cross-referencing every documented claim against those three branches yields exactly the six, plus four passages about branch two that are unaffected and correctly left alone. (2) Failure-code census. I grepped all 17 codes the lint actually emits across 96 tracked text files, excluding fixtures, the guild archive, and databricks-api. Every hit outside the lint and its own suite lands in `machine-contracts.md` — already location six's file — except `frontmatter-single-line` in SKILL.md:388, migration.md:81, and migrate-scope.sh, all three about the migrator's Tier 2 apply rather than v1 lint scope. No new file. (3) File census. The skill is 32 tracked files plus 2 under `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory`, so this is a census rather than a search: 22 of the 34 match none of the lexical vocabulary at all, and I swept those 22 for claim-bearing language independent of the words "v1," "lint," and "schema" — every hit is an unrelated sense of "migration." Also confirmed: no copy of these documents ships anywhere else in the repo. A fourth method would re-cover this ground. The reason the search can be declared closed is structural rather than statistical — the falsifiable surface is defined by the code, and the code branches on generation in exactly one place this job touches.
findings.evidence: Branches: lint-scope.sh:424 `if ! has_schema_key "$file"`, :451 `if ! has_v1_body "$file"`, :461 `grep -q '^memory_type:' "$file" || check_counts`. Branch-two passages, all still true post-fix: machine-contracts.md:19, SKILL.md:363, migrate-scope.sh:17-18, migration.md:103. Code census over 96 files for anchor-form, contradiction-fields, decision-fields, derived-counts, frontmatter-budget, frontmatter-fences, frontmatter-key-domain, frontmatter-key-order, frontmatter-known-keys, frontmatter-parses, frontmatter-single-line, link-broken, open-question-resolution, open-question-slug, tension-deferred-pairing, tension-fields, token-grammar. The 22 no-vocabulary files (templates, extraction-heuristics.md, memory-bank-schema.md, collapse-vtt.sh, eval-scope.sh) swept for `never (check|flag|fail)|not (check|flag)ed|generation|legal|old (note|file)|migrat`; three hits, all the business or memory-bank sense of "migration." `git ls-files | grep -iE 'machine-contracts|migration\.md|lint-scope'` returns one copy of each.

findings.description: The third sweep turned up something T-003's worker should have and does not: the repo already ships a generation-agnostic link check, in a sibling script, using the identical resolution order. `verify-migration.sh:123-165` reads every `.md` in the scope's git tree at `--since`, resolves each wiki target by filename and then by the trailing ten-character id, and never consults `schema` at any point. That is `check_links`' algorithm applied to v1 and v2 alike, shipped and passing today. It is the strongest available evidence that the lint's v1 exclusion was an accident of the pass-one `continue` rather than a design decision — which matters because C-10 requires the rewritten prose to carry the reason and not just the rule, and "the tool next door already does this to v1 files" is a better reason than anything currently in T-003's excerpt. Worth handing to the worker, with the note that `verify-migration.sh` is outside C-6's five-path allowlist and is therefore read-only material.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/scripts/verify-migration.sh:129-137 (`since_tree_targets`, which greps `\[\[[^]|]*` out of every `.md` at the ref with no generation filter), :151-160 (`find "$scope" -name "$target.md"`, then `id="${target: -10}"`), matching lint-scope.sh:375-377 exactly. Reported as `verify-link` at migration.md:144.

findings.description: Ruling on dispatching T-001 mid-audit: sound, and I would have done the same. r0 cleared T-001 on routing, worker isolation, and factual accuracy, which are the three things that decide whether a worker can start. Every finding in r1 and r2 has landed on T-003 or on the constitution's enumeration; not one has touched T-001's excerpt, its boundaries, or its checks. Under the serialization you adopted, T-001's slot was the only one that could run at all, so holding it would have bought nothing but latency. One qualification, and it is a process rule rather than a defect in this decomposition: r1's naming repair edited T-001's `check_method` after the task was dispatched, and T-001 is now at `checking` with a verdict of record already written. If that edit landed after the checker was briefed, the checker judged against text that no longer exists on disk, and a retrospective reading the task file will not be able to tell. The substance is harmless here — "seven-token" and "six-way" name the same block — but the rule worth carrying forward is that a task file is frozen once its agent is in flight: amendments wait for the agent to return, or force a re-dispatch, so that the artifact and the brief never diverge silently.
findings.evidence: T-001.md:36 `status: checking`; .agent-guild/state/verdicts/T-001-judgment-r0.json exists. T-001.md:17-19 carries the r1 naming repair. r0's per-task findings on T-001 were the boundary gap and two line citations, both repaired before dispatch; r1's only T-001 finding was the naming minor; r2 has none.

findings.description: Every r1 repair landed, verified against the files. C-8 enumerates six locations with the three consequences written into the clause, so a checker no longer has to reconstruct why the sixth matters. T-003 carries the title, a sixth section quoting the table and the sentence, and a C-8 check line reading "six." The preamble at constitution.md:3-5 now says six passages across four files and records that the count moved from four to five to six under audit, with the reason each addition was found — that is the right thing to have written down, because it makes the enumeration's provenance auditable instead of leaving the next reader to assume it came from the issue. T-003's caution is now complete and correctly framed: all four pinned surfaces listed, the `migration.md:610` refutation broken out separately with its inverted hazard stated plainly, the `lint-scope.sh` key-order pins and `bash -n` named, and the deletion-versus-proximity correction made explicitly rather than quietly. The lint-checks table is ruled out in T-003's Out of scope with reasoning that will survive a worker who disagrees, and it is distinguished from the generation table by name. T-001's injection block is described rather than counted, with the cross-reference to C-7's "six-way."
findings.evidence: constitution.md:3-5, :142-147; T-003.md:3, :13-17, :35, :77-93, :103, :105-112; T-001.md:17-19. C-6 correctly unchanged at five files — machine-contracts.md was already allowlisted, so location six needed no scope change.
